title: Technology-supported Risk Estimation by Predictive Assessment of Socio-technical Security Deliverable D2.3.2 TRESPASS Social data and policy extraction techniques
extended_summary:
This deliverable describes a set of methods and data sources for gathering and structuring social data for the TRESPASS socio-technical security model. The main problem addressed is how to collect context-rich social information that can be used to support risk assessment, attack-pattern modelling, and visualisation of information-sharing and information-protection practices. The document positions social data as essential for understanding the human and organisational relationships that shape security risk.

The paper presents several approaches, including GIS-based aggregation of census data for macro-level risk screening, participatory Stage-Zero risk assessments using rich pictures and LEGO-based modelling, narrative extraction from social engineering success stories, use of organisational records such as call-detail data, practitioner surveys on socio-technical cyber threats, and experimental techniques for testing cues and warnings against phishing. These approaches are framed as complementary ways to feed the TRESPASS Attack Navigator Map and attack pattern libraries.

The context is the TRESPASS project’s socio-technical security analysis, not an educational setting. The document emphasizes how different methods vary in breadth and granularity, and how they help analysts identify control strengths, vulnerabilities, and social practices across physical, digital, and organisational spaces. Its main conclusion is that combining these techniques can improve contextual understanding, support model refinement, and produce richer inputs for risk calculations and visualisations.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a project deliverable/grey-literature methods document rather than an empirical evaluation with learners. It contains descriptive case-method discussions but no clear experimental or comparative design and no peer-reviewed outcome evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper does not evaluate any K-12 educational intervention or report measurable learner impact. Its contributions are conceptual and methodological for socio-technical risk analysis, so educational impact is not demonstrated.

finding.finding_summary: This deliverable is a methods/grey-literature project report, not an intervention study. It proposes a framework for gathering social data for the TRESPASS model and describes how outputs feed the Attack Navigator Map, attack pattern libraries, and risk calculations, but it does not report outcome effects on learners.
finding.measure: Framework design outputs; descriptive utility for social data integration, risk mapping, and model refinement

finding.finding_summary: The document argues that the proposed techniques help security practitioners more efficiently scope scenarios, identify high-risk areas, and refine socio-technical risk models. For example, GIS-based aggregation is presented as a quick macro-level screening method to select high-risk areas for further analysis, but no quantitative productivity effect is reported.
finding.measure: Analyst workflow utility; ability to screen, scope, and refine risk models
